newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-STUTTGART REACH GERMAN CUP SEMIFINALS AFTER SHOOT-OUT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STUTTGART REACH GERMAN CUP SEMIFINALS AFTER SHOOT-OUT.

text.p: VfB Stuttgart had to play out most of extra time with 10 men before clinching their place in the semifinals of the German Cup after a penalty shoot-out with Freiburg on Wednesday.

Stuttgart, who are enjoying a superb season in the league where they are presently second, lost former international defender Thomas Berthold in the 94th minute after his second bookable offence of the night.

But the away side survived to win the quarter-final 4-2 on penalties. The two teams finished 90 minutes and extra time 1-1 after goals from VfB's striker Fredi Bobic and Freiburg's Martin Spanrin in the 48th and 63rd minutes.

Goalkeeper Joerg Schmadtke missed Bochum's opening penalty of the shoot-out before watching his opposite number Franz Wohlfahrt score a penalty and then save another from Swiss international Alain Sutter to seal the issue.
"That is the fourth time we have gone through after a shoot-out in this competition," Stuttgart coach Joachim Loew said. "We wanted to finish it off earlier to avoid testing the nerves.
"We had to show courage after Berthold's sending off and deserved to go through."

In the other quarter-final of the night, Argentine Rodolfo Cardoso, currently on loan from Werder Bremen, struck a late winner to put Hamburg into their first semifinal for eight years in a fortunate 2-1 home victory over Bochum.
Austrian Markus Schopp had given the UEFA Cup campaigners the lead at halftime after a 39th-minute goal before Peter Koezle equalized for Bochum in the 63rd minute.
Bochum were unlucky to go out since they played some good football in the second half and went close to sealing the issue.
"The best team lost this one. Everybody in the stadium saw that," Bochum coach Klaus Toppmoeller said. "It is very hard to deal with a defeat like this."
Regional league side Energie Cottbus became the first team to reach the last four when they upset first division St Pauli on Tuesday.
The last quarter-final between Karlsruhe and Bayern Munich will not take place until February 18. Bayern reached the last eight with a 3-1 victory over Bremen on Tuesday.
